clue.text: In the hollow, a pit in which to find a deer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'In the hollow, a pit in which to find a deer (6)': WAPITI is A PIT inside W...I (West Indies), but nothing in 'hollow' gives WI; likely an OCR garble of the printed abbreviation, no scan to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: In the hollow, a pit in which to find a deer

clue.text: Request to turn over during draw-go lightly

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie
PTO, please turn over, is the note asking a reader to flip the page

explanation.surface: Someone asks a player to flip a card during a game of draw, while moving gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw-go' hides a break: 'draw' gives TIE and 'go lightly' is the definition; 'during' puts PTO inside TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the balls of the feet is to move quietly and softly, stepping lightly.

clue.text: Observe local customs in part of Italy

definitions.text: Observe local customs in part of Italy

parts.words: Observe local customs in part of Italy
parts.note: the proverb about fitting in with your hosts, said originally of the Italian capital, is described literally here

explanation.surface: Advice to a tourist visiting a region of Italy to follow local habits.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb advises adopting the customs of the place you are visiting, with Rome as the example city.

clue.text: Still Reg, distraught outside, needs to get his own back

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters wrap around the other piece
distraught means upset and in disorder, so the letters of Reg are mixed up

parts.note: still, as in a calm sea, can mean even

explanation.surface: A man named Reg, though upset, is determined to retaliate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' scrambles REG into R...GE, and 'outside' puts that around EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to retaliate, paying back the person who harmed you.

clue.text: All (the males)

parts.note: an idiom meaning absolutely everybody, read literally as each mother's male child

explanation.surface: A bracketed note narrowing everyone to just the men.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single person, and literally names the boys born to every parent.

clue.text: When it's dropped, one cannot hear it

definitions.text: When it's dropped, one cannot hear it

parts.words: When it's dropped, one cannot hear it
parts.note: describes the breathy H sound that careless speakers drop, so it goes unheard

explanation.surface: Something that falls silently, making no noise as it lands.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one's aitches means leaving out the breathed H sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The breathy H sound is called this; when a speaker drops their aitches it is simply not voiced.

clue.text: Representative of French ambassador

parts.note: de is French for of
a legate is a papal envoy or ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone acting as an envoy for the French diplomatic service.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to act or vote for others, a representative.

clue.text: Lois came round in a vest

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Lois arrived wearing an undershirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the anagram signal: it turns LOIS CAME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's loose sleeveless undergarment, a kind of vest in British usage.

clue.text: Container ship?

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a container is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a receptacle such as a jug or bowl, and also a boat or ship.

clue.text: Letter opposing fifth-rate expedition leader

parts.note: V is short for versus, opposing
E is the fifth grade in a ranking A to E, so fifth-rate

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the word expedition

explanation.surface: A message criticising a second-rate head of an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Grades run A, B, C...: E, the fifth, stands for fifth-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter V spelt out in full.

clue.text: Aversion to the said test that had been rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dislike of a previously mentioned exam that was redone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the said test' reads as legal jargon, but only SAID TEST is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dislike or repugnance for something is an aversion.

clue.text: Complained bitterly, sudden attack having the French surrounded

indicators.note: surrounded says the raid goes round the French article

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone protested angrily after a surprise assault surrounded French troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something is to protest about it angrily.

clue.text: Let the cat out of the bag in play

definitions.text: Let the cat out of the bag in play

parts.words: Let the cat out of the bag in play
parts.note: revealing a secret while a match is under way, read as conceding the match itself

explanation.surface: Spilling a secret during a theatrical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret, and literally to concede a match while play continues.

clue.text: Against said girl taking the lead

parts.note: V for versus means against

indicators.note: said signals that the girl's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl, reportedly opposed, takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann spoken sounds like AN; the van is the front of an army, so being in the van is leading.
explanation.definitionFit: The van, short for vanguard, is the foremost position, the front.

clue.text: Lock up tribal leader first in the abbey

indicators.note: first says this letter is placed before the other piece
leader takes the opening letter of the word tribal

parts.note: to intern is to confine or lock up, especially in wartime

explanation.surface: A chieftain is imprisoned in a monastery before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: TINTERN Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey in Wales, made famous by a Wordsworth poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern is the name of a celebrated ruined monastery in the Wye Valley.

clue.text: Arouse interest in the plot

explanation.surface: Stirring curiosity about the storyline.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to fascinate; an intrigue is also a secret scheme or conspiracy.

clue.text: Grappling with a nail on a fish

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a tack is a small nail
ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Wrestling with a nail stuck into a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to grapple with it, getting to grips.

clue.text: More inclined to be more pricey

explanation.surface: Something more likely to cost more money.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep describes a sharp slope and, informally, an excessive price, so the comparative fits both.

clue.text: In favour of support being curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a prop is a support

explanation.surface: Backing a measure while support is being reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro is the Latin-derived word for for, supporting a cause.

clue.text: Condition of one sectarian initially in the clutches of a terrorist

indicators.note: being in someone's clutches means being held inside their grip

parts.note: a Provo is a member of the Provisional IRA
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word sectarian

explanation.surface: The fate of a bigot captured by a terrorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the clutches of' places I and S inside PROVO, after PROV.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Big noise coming from the City

definitions.text: Big noise coming from the City

parts.words: Big noise coming from the City
parts.note: a loud bang from London's financial district, read as a surge in share prices there

explanation.surface: A loud explosion heard from central London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, Britain's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp rise in share prices is a boom, punningly a loud bang from the financial district.

clue.text: He cannot afford much food in the pub

indicators.note: in places the food within the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is an item of food

explanation.surface: A poor man who can buy only a little to eat at the inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper who begs has very little money and can pay for almost nothing.

clue.text: Get shipwrecked boat in

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up, so the letters of boat in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bring a wrecked boat in to shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get it.

clue.text: Oil mixed in continental wine? It's a fiddle

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters within the wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of oil are jumbled

explanation.surface: Adding oil to French wine is a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns OIL into IOL, which 'in' places inside VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle is an informal name for the violin.

clue.text: Old settler got his cocktail after six

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters follow the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of got his are mixed

explanation.surface: An elderly colonist had his drink after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' turns GOT HIS into IGOTH, placed after VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths were a Germanic people who settled in Gaul and Spain in late Roman times.

clue.text: Some are risking using a runner

indicators.note: some says only part of the words are taken, the run inside them

explanation.surface: A few people take chances by using a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Boy about to run off came back?

indicators.note: about says the boy's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of run are shuffled

explanation.surface: A lad who was about to flee then returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns RUN into URN, and 'about' puts TED round it; the question mark flags that turning round is a loose sense of coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn is to reverse direction, heading back the way one came.

clue.text: Scattered crop said to be occurring only here and there

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters of crop said are dispersed

explanation.surface: A crop sown thinly that grows in patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound signal, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic events happen at irregular intervals or in isolated places.
